title: Rag Baby's alimony troubles, later life, and comparison with Stein
summary: Hazel tells how he had to finish jobs when Rag Baby fled detectives, and judges him a better band drummer than showman Stein.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: When you played the dances, they used the snare drum and the bass drum too?

Well, when I first started, yes. Because, uh, another little story about Rag Baby. Uh, incidentally, he has a son who works in the quarter. Yeah. Yeah. Nah. Well, Rag Baby was, uh, he always had, uh, lady troubles. And, uh, he, he was, uh, he, he left his family. I think he had six, seven kids, something like that. And he left to pull out on the family. And the, the police were always hounding him, you know, for alimony. And, uh, my dad would have to carry me along because they, they had places like the Southern Park out, out, out near, uh, by St. John there. And he's picking up over the river at the, the Crescent Park. And, uh, there was no telling when the detectives were gonna show up and Rag Baby would have to jump over the fence and take off, you see. And then I'd have to, I'd have to finish the night for him. And, uh, uh, he, uh, then he left here and he went to Chicago. He was around Chicago for a good while. He opened up a music shop up there. And he was the kind of guy that if he came out to his, out to see him and he had a silk Pangee suit on or something like, which was style in those days, Shantong, you know. Yeah. You had something wrong with your automobile, he'd just jump underneath there with that silk suit on and then see what's the matter with it. And he finally got killed in an automobile accident in Chicago. Yeah. And he was, a very fine drummer, both parade and, and jazz. He was, uh, uh, well, among the musicians, he, he was, uh, better thought of as, as a jazz drummer than, than Stein, who was the guy in the palace who has all the reputation. But the, the, the thing with Stein was that he had, uh, he had nine pipes built in a, in a U shape and he had, oh, everything in the world. Yeah. And the chimes and the, the boats and whistles and the bells and everything. He had everything in the world on that thing. But the, uh, uh, Rag Baby was more of a drummer, not a, not a showman. Like the, the solos today, things like that. Well, he was more of a, of a band. He worked for the band rather than for himself.
